ITT Inc. is a diversified engineering and manufacturing group making highly engineered components: brake pads for trains and cars (Wolverine, KONI shock absorbers), pumps and valves, connectors and sealing and thermal technologies. Customers are rail, automotive, aerospace, energy and industrial manufacturers, mostly sold B2B. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, with roughly 11,000 employees and about 3.6 billion dollars of annual revenue; listed on the NYSE (ITT). Industrial supplier with little consumer brand awareness, though KONI has some motorsport and enthusiast recognition.

Jumia is the largest pan-African e-commerce platform, operating a marketplace, logistics network (Jumia Logistics) and payment service (JumiaPay) in markets including Nigeria, Egypt, Morocco, Kenya and Ivory Coast. It sells electronics, fashion and household goods from third-party sellers to consumers and earns commissions, fulfilment fees and advertising. Founded in 2012, headquartered in Lagos with corporate roots in Berlin, it listed on the NYSE (JMIA) in 2019. Well-known consumer brand across Africa with tens of millions of visitors, little recognition elsewhere.

KPN is the largest telecommunications and IT provider in the Netherlands, selling mobile, fixed broadband, TV and fibre connectivity to consumers under KPN, Telfort and Simyo brands, plus network, cloud and IT services to businesses and government. Headquartered in Rotterdam, formerly the state postal and telephone monopoly (PTT) and now listed on Euronext Amsterdam (KPN). It has about 10,000 employees and roughly 5.5 billion euros of annual revenue. Highly visible household brand in the Netherlands and a long-standing sports and events sponsor domestically.

Morrisons (Wm Morrison Supermarkets) is a UK supermarket chain with around 500 stores, one of the big four grocers, based in Bradford, West Yorkshire. It is unusually vertically integrated, owning food manufacturing sites and supplying wholesale customers including Amazon and McColl's. Founded in 1899 and listed until 2021, it was taken private by US private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in a deal worth about 10 billion pounds. Revenue is roughly 17 billion pounds with about 100,000 staff. Very high consumer visibility across the UK, with no presence outside it.

Restaurant Brands International is the parent of fast-food chains Burger King, Tim Hortons, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs, plus the Carrefour-licensed Burger King and Tim Hortons international franchising operations. It earns royalties and rent from franchisees across more than 120 countries and over 30,000 restaurants, with system sales above 40 billion dollars. Created in 2014 when Burger King merged with Tim Hortons, backed by 3G Capital and Berkshire Hathaway; headquartered in Toronto and listed on the NYSE and TSX (QSR). Massive global consumer brands that already do large sports and entertainment marketing.

Scala Data Centers is a Brazil-based developer and operator of hyperscale, sustainable colocation data centres, anchored by its large AI City campus in Rio Grande do Sul and sites around Sao Paulo. It serves cloud providers, large enterprises and AI workloads that lease power and space. Formerly Odata, it was acquired by DigitalBridge in 2021 and renamed Scala in 2021 to 2022. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, with Latin America expansion plans and funding above 1.2 billion dollars. B2B infrastructure business with little consumer brand awareness.

Sunstone Hotel Investors is a US real estate investment trust that owns upper-upscale and luxury hotels, typically managed by major brands such as Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt. It owns roughly 15 to 20 hotels in places like Hawaii, California, Florida and Boston, and earns revenue from hotel operations rather than from consumer brands. Based in Aliso Viejo, California, listed on the NYSE (SHO). Owner of hotel real estate, not a hotel brand, so consumer visibility is low; sponsorship fit is mainly hospitality and corporate hospitality.

Symbotic provides AI-enabled warehouse automation: robotic storage and retrieval systems that palletise and move cases for large retailers and distributors. Its largest customer is Walmart, which also owns a stake and supported its listing; other customers include Target, Albertsons and C&S Wholesale Grocers. Based in Wilmington, Massachusetts, it went public via a SPAC merger with SVF Investment Corp. in 2022 and trades on Nasdaq (SYM). Revenue exceeds 2 billion dollars. In 2025 it agreed to acquire Walmart's robotics unit. B2B technology with little public brand awareness.

Talgo is a Spanish manufacturer of intercity, regional and high-speed passenger trains, known for its lightweight articulated rolling stock and variable-gauge axle systems. Customers are national railways and operators such as Renfe, Deutsche Bahn, Amtrak and Saudi Railways, and it also provides maintenance. Founded in 1942 and headquartered near Madrid at Las Rozas, it is listed on the Madrid stock exchange. A Spanish state-backed consortium led by Sidenor took control in 2024 after a bid by Skoda was blocked. Little consumer brand awareness outside rail circles.

Terrion is a telecommunications company based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Crunchbase says it creates secure and sustainable communication solutions. Total funding is shown as roughly 1.26 billion dollars, an unusually large amount for a company with this profile, so figures should be verified. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Youxia Motors is a Chinese electric vehicle start-up based in the Minhang district of Shanghai, which designs and manufactures electric cars. It has raised around 1.3 billion dollars of funding according to Crunchbase, and was one of the many Chinese EV newcomers of the late 2010s, also known as Youxia X. Customers would be Chinese consumers. Limited brand awareness outside China and no confirmed volume production, so its current status should be checked before outreach.

Industrial Logistics Properties Trust is a US real estate investment trust that owns and leases industrial and logistics properties, mainly in Hawaii (Oahu land leases) and across the mainland United States. Tenants are warehouse, distribution and industrial users, including Amazon and FedEx. It was spun out of Select Income REIT in 2018 and is managed by The RMR Group, based in Newton, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (ILPT). B2B landlord with essentially no consumer brand awareness; weak sponsorship fit.

Brunswick Corporation is a US maker of recreational marine products and fitness equipment. Brands include Mercury Marine outboard engines, Sea Ray, Bayliner, Boston Whaler and Lund boats, Navico Group marine electronics (Simrad, Lowrance), and the Life Fitness and Cybex gyms equipment businesses. Customers are boat owners, dealers, boat builders and commercial gyms; annual revenue is about 5 to 6 billion dollars. Founded in 1845, headquartered in Mettawa, Illinois (earlier Lake Forest), listed on the NYSE (BC). Strong recreational brands and an existing marine racing presence.

BVI Medical is a manufacturer and marketer of specialised ophthalmic surgical devices, including cataract and retinal surgery instruments, intraocular lenses and glaucoma implants, sold to surgeons and hospitals worldwide. Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, it grew out of Beaver-Visitec International and is privately held and owned by private equity investors. B2B medical products with no consumer visibility; very limited sponsorship fit.

Colovore is a provider of high-density liquid-cooled colocation data centre space in Santa Clara, California, designed for AI and high-performance computing racks. Customers are cloud, internet and AI companies needing far more power per rack than conventional facilities. It was founded in about 2013 and has raised capital from investors including Digital Realty and Pacific Gas & Electric-related sources, with total funding shown as roughly 957 million dollars. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand profile.

Diamond Sports Group was the owner of the Bally Sports regional sports networks, which carried local broadcast rights for dozens of MLB, NBA and NHL teams. It was created in 2019 when Sinclair Broadcast Group bought 21 regional networks from Disney and Fox for 10.6 billion dollars. Based in Norfolk, Virginia, it filed for Chapter 11 in 2023 after cord-cutting and rights fee pressures and emerged in 2024 as Main Street Sports Group, rebranded FanDuel Sports Network. Revenue came from cable and satellite carriage fees and advertising. Formerly well known to sports fans in the United States.

Enova International is a US online lending and fintech company that provides short-term credit, installment loans, lines of credit and small business financing under brands such as CashNet, NetCredit, OnDeck and Headway Capital. Customers are non-prime consumers and small businesses, and it uses proprietary analytics for underwriting. Founded in 2004 as part of Cash America, spun out in 2014; headquartered in Chicago and listed on the NYSE (ENVA). Reports around 3 billion dollars of annual revenue, largely in the United States and Brazil. Moderate brand awareness among consumers who borrow.

FiberLight is a US provider of high-capacity fibre-optic network infrastructure, serving carriers, enterprises, government, data centres and wireless providers across several states, with major metro networks in Texas, Georgia, Virginia, Washington DC and the Pacific Northwest. Headquartered in Plano, Texas, it is privately held, funded by infrastructure investors, with funding shown at about 922 million dollars. Revenue is mainly leased dark fibre, wavelengths and backhaul. B2B telecom wholesaler with little consumer brand awareness.

Gamma is a Los Angeles-based media and music company founded in 2021 by Larry Jackson, former head of Apple Music and Interscope Geffen, which backs artists and creators through a record label, publishing and film and television ventures. It raised about 1 billion dollars in a 2021 deal with Apple, Hollywood financiers and other backers. Customers are audiences streaming music, and Gamma earns revenue from recorded music, rights and content deals. Mid-level brand awareness, with artist signings such as Usher and Mary J. Blige adjacent partners; entertainment-sector fit.

GLP (formerly Global Logistic Properties) is a Singapore-based global investment manager and operator focused on logistics real estate, data centres, renewables and related technology, with more than 100 billion dollars of assets under management. Customers are tenants such as e-commerce and 3PL firms, and investors in its funds. It was listed in Singapore until 2017 when a consortium led by Hillhouse and Chinese investors took it private; Singapore-based GLP Capital Partners operated separately, and the logistics business has since been partly sold to Blackstone and ESR. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Kakao Mobility is the South Korean ride-hailing and mobility arm of Kakao, operating Kakao T, the dominant taxi-hailing app in Korea, plus parking, navigation (Kakao Navi), bike and chauffeur services. Drivers and consumers use the app, and revenue comes from commissions, subscriptions and advertising. Spun out in 2016 and based in Seongnam, Gyeonggi-do, it received investment from Carlyle in 2018 and TPG-led funds. Kakao T has tens of millions of registered users and high consumer visibility in South Korea, but no presence in Western markets.

LeSEE is a concept electric car unveiled by Chinese tech group LeEco (LeTV) in 2016, an autonomous, high-performance electric vehicle meant to rival Tesla, and the Crunchbase entry is for this project in Beijing. LeEco's car and electric vehicle ambitions, including its stake in Faraday Future, ran into financial trouble in 2017 and the company restructured under founder Jia Yueting. Funding shown is about 1.08 billion dollars. Effectively a stalled concept project, not an operating consumer brand today.

Logisteed is a Japanese third-party logistics company, formerly Hitachi Transport System, offering contract logistics, freight forwarding, warehousing and supply chain services to manufacturers and retailers across Japan, Asia, Europe and North America. Based in Tokyo and now owned by the Kohlberg Kravis Roberts-backed buyout group after a 2022 purchase of Hitachi's stake. The Crunchbase figure of about 142 billion yen is a funding amount. It employs tens of thousands, and revenue exceeds 700 billion yen. B2B logistics brand with little public awareness; the Hitachi legacy name is better known.

Odata Brasil was a Brazilian data centre operator based in Sao Paulo, providing large-scale colocation facilities for cloud providers and enterprises. It was acquired by DigitalBridge in 2021 and rebranded Scala Data Centers, so it is the same business as the Scala Data Centers entry. Funding of about 1.08 billion dollars is shown. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness; sponsorship fit is weak.

Ozon is Russia's largest e-commerce platform, a multi-category marketplace selling electronics, fashion, groceries and household goods with its own logistics, a fintech arm (Ozon Bank) and a seller marketplace. Founded in 1998 and based in Moscow, it listed on Nasdaq in 2020, which was a first for a Russian internet company. Its Nasdaq trading was suspended after 2022 sanctions and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and the group was reorganised under Russian ownership. Tens of millions of active buyers and very high brand awareness in Russia, but no international reach and sanctions exposure.

Pet Valu is a Canadian specialty retailer of pet food and supplies, with roughly 800 corporate and franchise stores in Canada under the Pet Valu and Chico banners, plus the Hartz Cats and Dogs selling business and online sales. Customers are pet owners buying premium food, treats and accessories. Founded in 1976 and headquartered in Markham, Ontario; listed on the TSX (PET) since 2021. Revenue is about 1.2 billion Canadian dollars. Well known Canadian consumer brand but with no presence in the other F1 markets.

POOLCORP (Pool Corporation) is the world's largest wholesale distributor of swimming pool supplies, equipment and outdoor living products, operating roughly 450 service centers across North America, Europe and Australia under names such as SCP, Superior Pool Products and Horizon. Customers are pool builders, retailers and service professionals rather than consumers. Based in Covington, Louisiana and listed on Nasdaq (POOL). Annual sales are about 5.5 billion dollars. B2B distributor with limited consumer brand awareness.

Real Madrid C.F. is the Spanish football club, member-owned and based in Madrid, 15-time European Cup and Champions League winner and one of the most valuable sports franchises globally, with annual revenue above 1 billion euros. It earns income from matchday, broadcasting, commercial sponsorships and merchandising at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium, plus basketball and other sports. Its global following runs into hundreds of millions; sponsors include Emirates, Adidas and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Very high consumer visibility; already an elite sponsor-seeking property that may compete with F1 for budgets.

Salt Mobile (formerly Orange Switzerland, rebranded in 2015) is Switzerland's third-largest mobile network operator, serving about 1.7 million mobile customers and growing fixed fibre and home broadband under Salt and Salt Home brands. Headquartered in Prilly near Lausanne, it is owned by French billionaire Xavier Niel's investment vehicle NJJ, which bought it in 2014 and has taken it private. It offers prepaid and postpaid plans. Strong consumer brand awareness in Switzerland, known for aggressive pricing, but with no international footprint.

Singulato Motors is a Chinese electric vehicle start-up founded in 2014 by Shen Haiyin, former head of Wanxiang's EV unit, and based in China. The Crunchbase entry lists it in Santa Clara, California with a Chinese parent operation. It planned to build smart electric cars, including the iS6 SUV, and reported raising over 1 billion dollars from investors including Hillhouse and CITIC. It failed to reach volume production and has been largely inactive since around 2019 to 2020, so its current status should be verified before outreach.

TKO Group Holdings is the US sports and entertainment company formed in 2023 by combining UFC and WWE under Endeavor's control, listed on the NYSE (TKO). It owns the Ultimate Fighting Championship, World Wrestling Entertainment, PBR (bull riding) and the Zuffa Boxing venture, and earns revenue from media rights, live events, sponsorships and licensing. Based in New York, with Endeavor as majority owner, and combined revenue of around 3 billion dollars or more. Large global fan base and heavy sponsorship activity, making it a peer sports property as well as a potential partner.

Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG) was Uber's self-driving car research unit, based in Pittsburgh, building autonomous vehicles and lidar for robotaxi services. It raised 1 billion dollars in 2019 from SoftBank, Toyota and Denso, valuing the unit at about 7.25 billion dollars. After a fatal pedestrian crash in Arizona in 2018, it was sold to Aurora Innovation in December 2020 in a deal that left Uber holding a stake in Aurora. No longer operating as an independent company; no active consumer brand.

Banma Network Technologies is a Shanghai-based Chinese internet-car software company, a joint venture of Alibaba and SAIC Motor founded in 2015, which builds the Banma Zhixing operating system and connected services for cars such as the SAIC Roewe RX5, with Alibaba's AliOS technology. Customers are automakers, and it has been funded by Alibaba, SAIC and investors, with funding shown at about 4.6 billion yuan. B2B software supplier; consumer awareness is low and tied to the cars it powers, mostly in China.

Caocao Chuxing (Cao Cao Mobility) is a Chinese ride-hailing company launched in 2015 and backed by automaker Geely, operating a fleet of electric cars on its own app in Hangzhou and over 100 Chinese cities. It earns fares and commissions and uses Geely-built electric vehicles and its own charging network. Spun out of Geely, it listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in June 2025. Brand awareness is regional in China, mainly among riders in Chinese cities; it competes with Didi. Funding shown is about 4.8 billion yuan before its IPO.

Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance (Ant Consumer Finance) is a licensed Chinese consumer finance company established in Chongqing in 2020, majority controlled by Ant Group and Chongqing financial interests, offering consumer loans through Alipay platforms such as Huabei (Ant Credit Pay) and Jiebei. It lends to individuals in China and had registered capital of around 8 billion yuan, with funding shown at 6 billion yuan. Strong brand exposure through the Ant and Alipay ecosystem within China only, and under strict financial regulation.

Einride is a Swedish freight technology company founded in 2016, known for its electric and autonomous trucks (the pod without a cab) and a freight-as-a-service platform with a logistics software layer. Customers include Maersk, Lidl, GE Appliances, Oatly and Bridgestone, and it operates in Sweden, the US and Europe. Based in Stockholm, it is backed by Nordic investors, EQT and Temasek-linked sources, and announced a SPAC merger with Legato Merger Corp. III in 2025 to list in the US. B2B but with visible branding on its futuristic trucks.

Groupe SEB is the French small domestic appliances and cookware group behind Tefal, Krups, Rowenta, Moulinex, Seb, WMF, Lagostina and Supor. It sells kitchen, home-care and personal care products through retailers and professional coffee machines to commercial customers in 150 countries, with sales above 8 billion euros and about 33,000 employees. Founded in 1857, headquartered in Ecully near Lyon (Crunchbase shows Carros), listed on Euronext Paris (SK), with the Peugeot-family holding company FFP and Venelle controlling shares. Household brands with broad consumer recognition worldwide.

Inspired Entertainment is a global gaming technology company supplying server-based gaming machines, virtual sports, digital games and interactive content to casinos, betting shops, lotteries and online operators. Customers are regulated gambling operators in the UK, Italy, North America and other markets, and it earns revenue from leased terminals and game licensing. Its virtual sports were once used by UK bookmakers such as William Hill and Ladbrokes. Headquartered in New York with large UK operations, listed on Nasdaq (INSE), with revenue around 300 million dollars. B2B gambling supplier with limited consumer brand awareness; regulated sector.

InterVest Capital Partners is a New York-based asset-based lender, according to the Crunchbase description, providing consumer and commercial financing. Crunchbase industries list consumer and financial services. The funding amount shown is 867 million dollars. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

IQM Quantum Computers is a Finnish company that builds superconducting quantum computers, selling full-stack systems and on-premises quantum machines to supercomputing centres, universities and research labs, along with cloud access. Spun out of Aalto University and VTT in 2018, it is based in Espoo and has operations in Munich and elsewhere. It has raised over 600 million dollars, including a 320 million dollar round in 2025 led by Ten Eleven Ventures, and is one of Europe's best-funded quantum companies. B2B deep-tech with little general consumer awareness.

Merama is a Mexican e-commerce aggregator, founded in 2021, that acquires and scales Amazon and online brands in Latin America, particularly in Mexico, Brazil and Colombia. It provides funding, operational expertise and resources to sellers, and it earns money by owning and selling consumer products across home, beauty and sports categories through online marketplaces. Based in Mexico City, it raised hundreds of millions of dollars in venture and debt financing. Limited direct brand recognition because the brands it owns are marketed separately.

Myntra is an Indian online fashion and lifestyle marketplace founded in 2007, headquartered in Bengaluru and owned by Flipkart, which acquired it in 2014 and also owns its sister brand Jabong. It sells clothing, footwear and accessories from thousands of brands, runs its own private labels like Roadster and HRX, and hosts the End of Reason Sale. Customers are consumers across India, with tens of millions of users. Strong consumer brand in India; Flipkart, in turn, is majority owned by Walmart.

The New England Patriots are the National Football League franchise in Foxborough, Massachusetts, owned by the Kraft family since 1994, and winners of six Super Bowls during the Tom Brady and Bill Belichick era. The team plays at Gillette Stadium and revenue comes from NFL broadcasting rights, sponsorship, ticketing and merchandise. The franchise is valued at roughly 7 billion dollars or more. The Kraft Group also owns MLS club New England Revolution. Very high US consumer visibility and an existing global fan base, notably in the UK and Germany through NFL international games.

Nexperia is a Dutch semiconductor manufacturer, headquartered in Nijmegen, producing discrete devices, logic chips and MOSFETs supplied mainly to the automotive sector as well as industrial and consumer electronics customers. It was spun off from NXP in 2017 and acquired by Chinese-owned Wingtech Technology, with the Dutch government intervening in the company's control in late 2025 over national security concerns, triggering supply disruption for carmakers. About 12,000 employees. B2B component supplier with little public brand awareness.

Polaris Inc. is a US manufacturer of powersports vehicles: off-road vehicles (RZR, Ranger, General), snowmobiles, Indian Motorcycle, Slingshot three-wheelers, Polaris boats and defence vehicles through Polaris Government and Defense. Sales are about 7 billion dollars annually and customers are consumers, dealers and military buyers, sold in North America and overseas. Founded in 1954 in Roseau, Minnesota, headquartered in Medina, Minnesota (Crunchbase shows Ohio) and listed on the NYSE (PII). Strong consumer brand in motorsports and outdoor recreation, with a long history of racing sponsorships.

Qifu Technology (formerly 360 DigiTech) is a Chinese credit-tech platform operating the 360 Jietiao app, which connects consumers and small business owners with banks and licensed financial institutions through loan facilitation, risk-management services and insurance. It was spun from Qihoo 360 and is based in Shanghai, listed on Nasdaq (QFIN) since 2018. Revenue is several billion yuan per year. Strong brand exposure to Chinese borrowers, but limited presence outside China, and sector subject to heavy regulation.

Samsung SDS is the IT services and logistics arm of the Samsung group, founded in 1985 and headquartered in Seoul. It provides cloud, system integration, AI, cybersecurity and smart-factory services, plus the Cello Square logistics platform and the Brity enterprise automation brands. Customers are mainly Samsung affiliates and increasingly other large enterprises and governments. It is listed on the Korea Exchange (018260), with Samsung C&T and Samsung Electronics the main shareholders, and revenue around 13 trillion won. B2B, limited consumer awareness, though the Samsung family name is globally strong.

SEGG Media Corporation is a US-listed holding company, based in Spicewood, Texas, formerly Lottery.com, a lottery ticket management and online lottery platform. It has been repositioned toward sports, media and gaming, including a Spanish sports media and marketing business associated with sports stars, and its share listing is on Nasdaq (SEGG). It has had a turbulent history, including an SEC investigation, and a very small revenue base. Funding shown is about 774 million dollars, which looks inflated by non-standard financing. Limited brand awareness; treat with caution on credibility.

Voyah is the premium electric vehicle brand of Dongfeng Motor Group, a Chinese state-owned automaker, selling the Free, Dreamer, Passion and Chaser models in China and abroad. It is sold in markets including Norway, where the Crunchbase entry places its European headquarters in Oslo, with exports across Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Customers are consumers and fleets buying plug-in hybrid and electric vehicles. Dongfeng restructured its listing in Hong Kong and moved Voyah toward a 2025 Hong Kong listing via a reverse takeover. Moderate consumer awareness in China, still building in Europe.

WASH is a US laundry room management company, historically known as WASH Multifamily Laundry Systems, which supplies and services coin and app-operated washers and dryers in apartment buildings, student housing and hospitality. Customers are property owners and managers, and it shares laundry revenue with them. Headquartered in Torrance, California, it is owned by private equity and large investors (Crunchbase shows funding of about 850 million dollars). Large route-based operator in more than 40 states. Recognised by residents on site but little general consumer brand awareness.

Winbond Electronics is a Taiwanese semiconductor company that designs, manufactures and sells memory chips: serial flash, specialty DRAM and secure flash, used in automotive, industrial, consumer electronics and telecom products. It operates its own fabs in Taichung and Kaohsiung, Taiwan, and is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2344), founded in 1987 and part of the Walsin Lihwa group. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. B2B component supplier with limited consumer visibility.

Xponential Fitness is a US franchisor of boutique fitness studios, including Club Pilates, Pure Barre, CycleBar, Rumble, YogaSix, StretchLab and Lindora, with around 3,000 studios worldwide. It earns franchise fees, royalties and equipment sales from franchisees and serves consumers who pay memberships. Headquartered in Irvine, California, it listed on the NYSE (XPOF) in 2021 and has faced litigation and an SEC probe over the company's franchise sales practices. Strong consumer brand names in US boutique fitness, expanding internationally.

Zilch is a UK fintech offering interest-free buy-now-pay-later at checkout and a virtual Mastercard, funded in part by advertising and by merchant fees rather than consumer interest. Founded in 2018, it is headquartered in London, with customers across the UK and Europe and a licence in the US. It has raised funding from Goldman Sachs and other investors and reached a valuation of more than 2 billion dollars. Known to UK consumers through its high-profile marketing and sponsorships, including football and sports partnerships.

ADMIE Holding is the Greek holding company for IPTO, the independent power transmission operator that runs and maintains Greece's high-voltage electricity grid, including interconnections to Italy, Bulgaria and Turkey. Revenue comes from regulated transmission fees. Headquartered in Athens and listed on the Athens Stock Exchange (ADMIE), it is controlled by the Greek state through DES ADMIE, while State Grid Corporation of China holds 24 percent. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

ATI Physical Therapy is a US operator of outpatient orthopedic physical therapy clinics, with roughly 900 clinics in 25 states, treating injuries, post-surgery rehabilitation and sports medicine. Revenue comes from insurance and patient payments, and the company works with physicians and employers. Headquartered in Downers Grove, Illinois, it went public through a SPAC merger with Fortress Value Acquisition Corp. II in 2021, trading on the NYSE (ATIP), and later struggled with performance issues. Known regionally as a local healthcare brand; limited national consumer awareness.

HengTen Networks Group is a Hong Kong-listed holding company, formerly China Network Media, linked to Tencent and Evergrande Group, which invested in internet services, applications and later in Chinese property, and later moved into real estate and online game businesses. Headquartered in Wan Chai, Hong Kong; funding shown is around 5 billion Hong Kong dollars. Its prominence faded after the Evergrande group collapse. B2B and investment oriented with little consumer brand visibility.

Hoist Finance is a Swedish credit management and debt restructuring company that buys non-performing consumer loans from banks and works with debtors to arrange repayment, in markets including the UK, France, Italy, Spain and Poland. It also operates a regulated savings bank, taking deposits in Sweden and Germany. Headquartered in Stockholm and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (HOFI), it was founded in 1994 and has around 1,000 employees. Low consumer brand awareness since customers typically do not choose it.

Jazz is Pakistan's largest mobile operator and digital services company, with around 70 million subscribers, offering mobile voice and data, JazzCash digital payments, and Jazz World content. Owned by VEON Group, which listed on Nasdaq, and based in Islamabad, it was formed from the merger of Mobilink and Warid in 2016. Revenue is hundreds of billions of Pakistani rupees. A major consumer brand in Pakistan with heavy sports and cricket sponsorship (including the Pakistan Super League), but no presence outside it.

Lunar is a Danish digital bank, founded in 2015 in Copenhagen and operating in Denmark, Sweden and Norway, offering mobile-first accounts, loans, savings, business banking and investment products through its app. It has about 500,000 customers, is backed by Index Ventures, Lunar's founders and others, and has raised over 500 million dollars. Holds a Danish banking licence. Known to Nordic consumers with active youthful marketing, but not known outside Scandinavia.

Muangthai Capital is a Thai non-bank finance company that provides motorcycle, vehicle title and personal loans to consumers and small business owners, mostly in rural areas through a network of several thousand branches. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (MTC), headquartered in Bangkok and founded in 1992. Customers are low- to middle-income individuals. Strong regional name recognition in Thailand with branch-based marketing, but nothing internationally.

PayJoy is a San Francisco fintech that finances smartphone purchases for people with limited credit history in emerging markets, using a lock-and-unlock technology that restricts the phone if payments stop. It operates in Mexico, Brazil, India, South Africa, Indonesia, Colombia and the US, working with retail partners, and has financed millions of phones. Founded in 2015, it has raised several hundred million dollars in equity and debt from Andreessen Horowitz, Valar and others. Little consumer brand recognition outside the sales channel.

Scalable Capital is a German digital wealth manager and neo-broker based in Munich, offering ETF savings plans, automated investment portfolios (Scalable Wealth) and commission-free trading (Scalable Broker). It serves retail investors in Germany, Austria and other European markets, and has over a million customers and tens of billions of euros under management. Founded in 2014, it is backed by BlackRock, HV Capital, Tengelmann and Tencent. Moderate consumer awareness in German-speaking markets, with online advertising and some sports sponsorship.

Stash is a US consumer fintech app that offers investing, banking, retirement accounts and financial education, targeting beginners, with fractional shares and auto-investing from small amounts. It has several million customers and revenue from monthly subscriptions. Headquartered in New York, founded in 2015, it has raised nearly 700 million dollars from investors including Union Square Ventures, Goodwater Capital and Coatue. Known to US consumers through national advertising and partnerships but still a niche brand.

Storebrand is one of the largest Norwegian financial services groups, providing pensions, life insurance, asset management, savings and banking to individuals, corporations and public sector. It manages over 1 trillion Norwegian kroner, is headquartered in Lysaker near Oslo and listed on Euronext Oslo (STB). Founded in 1767, it has been an early mover in sustainable investing. Strong brand in Norway with sports sponsorships (including football), but regional.

Xepelin is a Chilean fintech platform that provides working capital financing, invoice factoring and financial management software to small and mid-size businesses across Latin America, in Chile, Mexico and Colombia. Founded in 2019 in Santiago, it earns interest and fees from the financing and has raised over 600 million dollars in equity and debt from Kaszek, Valor Capital, Tiger Global and others. B2B brand, familiar mainly within the Latin American startup and SME community.

Absci is a US synthetic biology and drug discovery company that uses generative AI and cell engineering to design antibody and protein drugs, partnering with pharmaceutical firms such as Almirall and AstraZeneca while building its own pipeline (including ABS-101 and ABS-201). Founded in 2011 and based in Vancouver, Washington, it listed on Nasdaq (ABSI) in 2021. Revenue is small and from partnerships. B2B biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Aditya Birla Housing Finance is an Indian housing finance company, a subsidiary of Aditya Birla Capital, offering home loans, loans against property, construction finance and lease rental discounting to individuals and developers across India. Part of the Aditya Birla Group, headquartered in Mumbai. Customers are home buyers and property owners; revenue is net interest income. Recognised by Indian borrowers via the broader Aditya Birla brand, which has a large consumer name in India.

AIXTRON SE is a German manufacturer of metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) equipment used to produce compound semiconductors, such as LEDs, power electronics, lasers and communication chips for makers of silicon carbide and gallium nitride devices. Customers are chipmakers and research labs, mainly in Asia. Founded in 1983 and headquartered in Herzogenrath near Aachen, it is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (AIXA, also in the TecDAX). Annual revenue is about 600 million euros. B2B equipment supplier with little consumer visibility.

Alto Neuroscience is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company using brain biomarkers and AI to match patients to treatments for psychiatric conditions such as depression, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Its drug candidates include ALTO-100, ALTO-300 and ALTO-203. Based in Mountain View, California, it listed on the NYSE (ANRO) in early 2024 after raising hundreds of millions in venture funding. Pre-revenue biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Pipe is a San Francisco fintech platform that lets companies with recurring revenue, such as subscription software businesses, sell future revenue streams for upfront capital, and trade them with investors. Founded in 2019, it has raised about 450 million dollars in equity and debt from investors including Greenspring, Shopify and others. B2B financial platform with limited consumer awareness.

RapidSOS is a New York public safety technology company whose platform delivers emergency data, such as location and medical information from phones, cars and wearables, to 911 call centres and first responders. It works with Apple, Google, Uber and many carmakers, and is used across thousands of US emergency centres. Founded in 2012, it has raised about 455 million dollars. B2B and government customer base with modest consumer awareness.

REC Silicon is a Norwegian-listed (Oslo, RECSI) producer of polysilicon and silane gas, with its main US plant at Moses Lake, Washington, supplying solar, electronics and semiconductor customers. It was founded in 1996 in Norway. Hanwha Solutions acquired a majority shareholding in 2021 and the Moses Lake plant has been affected by Chinese competition and tariffs; production was curtailed in 2025. B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Regents Capital Corporation is a financial services company based in Costa Mesa, California. Crunchbase lists commercial and crowdfunding among its industries and describes it as providing financial services. Funding shown is about 413 million dollars. Its exact business and ownership are not clear from the information provided. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Reliable Robotics is a Mountain View aviation technology company developing automated flight systems that let cargo aircraft such as the Cessna 208 Caravan fly with remote pilots on the ground. The company works with the FAA and the US Air Force and has partnered with cargo operators, including regional cargo carriers. Founded in 2017, it has raised about 410 million dollars from investors including Eclipse and Lightspeed. B2B aviation technology with some visibility in the aerospace sector.

Rhoda AI is a Palo Alto start-up developing a class of robotics foundation models, which allow robots to learn tasks from video and demonstration. Founded recently and backed by prominent venture investors, it has funding of about 450 million dollars shown. Customers would be industrial and logistics operators. B2B and early-stage, with little consumer awareness.

Rox Resources is an Australian ASX-listed (RXL) exploration and development company, focused on the Youanmi gold project in Western Australia and nickel and gold prospects in the Northern Territory and the Mount Fisher area. It does not yet generate material revenue. Based in Perth, it is funded by equity raisings and investors. B2B resources developer with no consumer brand awareness.

Scale Computing is an Austin-based provider of edge computing and hyperconverged infrastructure, with its HyperCore software and SC//Platform for retailers, manufacturers, schools and government sites that need simple on-site IT. Customers include thousands of small and mid-sized organisations plus resellers. Founded in 2007, it has raised funding of about 437 million dollars. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

SEALSQ is a Swiss-based semiconductor and post-quantum cryptography company that makes secure chips, secure elements and tamper-proof identity technology for IoT, satellites and payments. It is a spin-off of WISeKey, headquartered in Geneva, with operations in Meyreuil, France, and is listed on Nasdaq (LAES). Customers are electronics and device manufacturers. Small revenue and high losses. B2B with low consumer awareness.

SiEngine Technology is a Shanghai-based Chinese company that designs automotive-grade chips, including the Dragon Eagle series of smart cockpit system-on-chips used in cars from Geely and other makers. It was founded by Geely-related interests in 2018 and has raised funding of about 420 million dollars. Customers are Chinese carmakers. B2B component designer with no consumer brand awareness.

SignSplit is a New York platform described by Crunchbase as a data and infrastructure platform in the blockchain and content delivery sectors. Funding shown is about 400 million dollars, which looks unusually high and may be mis-read. Nothing else about products, customers or ownership can be confirmed from the data supplied. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The Sapir Organization is a New York real estate group founded by Tamir Sapir and run by his son Alex Sapir, a company with development and investment interests in hospitality and property, and known for the Trump SoHo hotel development with Donald Trump's company, and for property holdings in the US and Eastern Europe. Crunchbase describes it as a group of privately and publicly held companies. Reported funding is about 431 million dollars. Low consumer awareness.

Vena Solutions is a Toronto software company offering a cloud platform for corporate finance, covering budgeting, planning, forecasting and consolidation, built around Microsoft Excel. Customers include mid-sized and large enterprises in sectors like manufacturing, healthcare and finance. Founded in 2002, it has raised funding of about 418 million dollars, mostly from Battery Ventures and Summit Partners. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

Volta Trucks was a London- and Stockholm-based electric commercial truck start-up that designed the Volta Zero, a full-electric 16-tonne truck for city deliveries, and sold it to fleet customers such as DFDS and Heineken. It began production in Steyr, Austria in 2022, but suffered a major safety recall and financing problems, and entered administration in 2023, with its assets later acquired by Luxor, a Chinese-linked investor in 2024. B2B commercial vehicle brand, now defunct as an independent business.

Vosker is a Canadian company based in Victoria, Quebec, developing remote-area monitoring technology that uses solar-powered cameras with AI to watch large outdoor sites such as farms, mines and forests. Funding of about 450 million dollars is shown, which seems unusually large and may be an OCR error. Customers are rural land and infrastructure operators. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

Yunxuetang is a Suzhou-based Chinese enterprise learning company providing a comprehensive online training platform for corporate employees, with content, learning management and talent development tools. Customers are companies across China, including large state and private enterprises. It has funding of about 390 million dollars. B2B software with little profile outside China and no consumer brand awareness.

Allbirds is a San Francisco footwear and apparel brand known for its Wool Runner and Tree Runner sneakers made from merino wool and eucalyptus fibre, with a sustainability and carbon-footprint-labelling angle. It sells through its own stores and website, plus wholesale, in the US, Europe and Asia, and listed on Nasdaq (BIRD) in 2021 at a valuation above 2 billion dollars. Founded in 2016, it has since seen collapsing sales and a much lower valuation. Widely recognised lifestyle consumer brand, particularly in the US.

Amara Raja is an Indian industrial group, based in Tirupati and Hyderabad, best known for Amaron car and Quanta industrial lead-acid batteries and also in lithium cell manufacturing, EV charging and power electronics. The Galla family and Johnson Controls were major shareholders. Listed on the NSE and BSE as Amara Raja Energy & Mobility. Revenue is more than 12,000 crore rupees. Amaron is a well-known consumer automotive battery brand in India, with cricket and sports sponsorships.

Arsenale Group is an Italian multi-brand hospitality and travel group based in Rome, with a portfolio of hotels and resorts, including properties in Italy and other tourist destinations. The Crunchbase description says it provides a multi-brand offer, and funding shown is around 300 million euros. Customers are leisure and business travellers. Brand awareness is mainly regional.

Celero Commerce is a Nashville payments and commerce technology company providing integrated payment processing, point-of-sale software and merchant services to small and mid-sized businesses, including restaurants, retailers and healthcare practices, through sales partners and software vendors. It earns processing fees and software subscriptions. Funding shown is about 375 million dollars. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

ClearMotion is a Billerica, Massachusetts automotive technology company that makes active ride systems, using electromechanical actuators and software to cancel road vibration and body motion in cars, and has been developing the Activalve smart damper for car makers. Founded in 2009 as Levant Power, it has raised about 360 million dollars from investors including Qatar-linked and Chinese auto interests. Customers are automakers; B2B with low consumer awareness.

Coca-Cola Beverages Florida is a Tampa-based bottler and distributor of Coca-Cola products across much of Florida, manufacturing and delivering soft drinks, water, juices and energy drinks to supermarkets, restaurants and convenience stores. It is one of the large regional Coca-Cola bottlers in the United States, operating production plants and distribution depots with thousands of employees. B2B route-to-market business under the globally famous Coca-Cola brand, but little standalone consumer brand awareness.

Four Seasons Hotel and Residences Jacksonville is a luxury hotel and branded residences development in Jacksonville, Florida, under the Four Seasons brand, announced as part of a large waterfront mixed-use project. Funding shown is about 360 million dollars. Customers are luxury leisure and business travellers and residential buyers. The Four Seasons brand has very high recognition among affluent consumers; this particular property is a local development.

Nokian Tyres is a Finnish tyre manufacturer, based in Nokia near Tampere, known for winter tyres and the invention of the winter tyre in 1934, selling passenger car, van, truck and agricultural tyres under the Nokian and Vianor retail brands. It has factories in Finland, the United States (Dayton, Tennessee) and Romania, and is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (TYRES). Revenue is about 1.3 billion euros. Strong in the Nordics and North America with motorsport and rally associations.

Onto is a London-based electric vehicle subscription service, rebranded in 2021 from the UK arm of US car subscription company Fair, which offers cars from Tesla, Polestar, Kia and others on flexible monthly contracts including insurance, servicing and charging. Customers are UK consumers and businesses wanting to avoid ownership. It was backed by Fair's investors such as SoftBank, with funding of about 369 million dollars shown. Moderate consumer awareness in the UK.

OVS S.p.A. is an Italian fashion retailer, with around 1,000 stores of the OVS, OVS Kids and Upim brands, selling affordable clothing for men, women and children, and the Stefanel brand after a later acquisition. Customers are mass-market Italian consumers, with growing international franchising. Founded in 1972 as part of Coin group and headquartered in Venice-Mestre, it listed on the Milan stock exchange (OVS) in 2015. Revenue is over 1.5 billion euros. Very well known household retail brand in Italy.

Savers Value Village is a for-profit thrift retailer with over 300 stores in the United States, Canada and Australia, operating as Savers, Value Village, Unique Thrift and Village des Valeurs. It sells second-hand clothing, accessories and household goods, sourced mainly from donations collected through paid partnerships with non-profit organisations. Based in Bellevue, Washington, it is controlled by Ares Management and listed on the NYSE (SVV) since 2023. Revenue is about 1.5 billion dollars. Strong recognition among North American thrift shoppers.

Yatsen Holding is a Chinese beauty group behind Perfect Diary, Little Ondine, Abby's Choice, Galenic and DR.WU, selling cosmetics and skincare mainly through online channels such as Tmall, Douyin and its own stores. Founded in 2016 and based in Guangzhou, it listed on the NYSE (YSG) in 2020. Revenue is around 4 billion yuan, down from peak levels, as competition in Chinese beauty has intensified. Perfect Diary is a prominent consumer brand with celebrity endorsements in China.

Athletic Brewing is a Connecticut-based producer of non-alcoholic craft beer, with brands such as Run Wild IPA, Upside Dawn and Free Wave Hazy IPA, brewed at facilities in Milford, Connecticut and San Diego. Founded in 2017, it sells through grocery, bars and online, and is the largest non-alcoholic craft brewer in the United States, with sales around 100 million dollars or more. It raised funding of about 300 million dollars from investors including Spectrum Equity. Growing consumer brand with a sports and wellness image.

BarkBox (BARK, Inc.) is a US pet products company that sells monthly BarkBox toy and treat subscriptions, Super Chewer boxes for heavy chewers and BarkBox Dental, along with the Bark Eats and Bark Supplies lines for the retail market. Based in New York with a distribution base in Ohio, it listed on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in 2021 and has revenue of about 450 million dollars. Customers are dog owners; subscription and e-commerce sales. Recognisable consumer brand among US pet owners.

FlashEX (Shansong) is a Beijing-based Chinese intracity express delivery service that uses a crowdsourced network of couriers to deliver parcels, documents and food within hours, on a demand basis. Its customers are consumers and businesses in major Chinese cities, and it has raised about 289 million dollars. Competes with Dada and other local delivery players. Brand awareness is largely limited to Chinese city dwellers.

Fresha is a London-based booking and business software platform for the beauty and wellness industry, used by salons, barbers and spas to manage appointments, point of sale and payments, with a consumer marketplace for booking appointments. Software is free to businesses, and it earns from payment processing and marketplace fees. Formerly Shedul, founded in 2015, it serves hundreds of thousands of professionals in over 120 countries. Backed by General Atlantic and Temasek. Known to beauty professionals and consumers using its app.

Glossier is a New York direct-to-consumer beauty brand founded by Emily Weiss in 2014 from the Into The Gloss blog, selling minimalist skincare and make-up such as Boy Brow, Cloud Paint and Balm Dotcom online, in its own stores and, from 2022, through Sephora. Customers are mainly young women, and it is known for community-driven marketing. It raised over 300 million dollars at a valuation of 1.8 billion dollars in 2019. Weiss stepped back in 2022 and Kyle Leahy became CEO. Strong consumer brand with a loyal following.

Ionik is a Toronto, Ontario company described by Crunchbase as a performance marketing technology company in the gaming and online games sector. Funding shown is about 308 million dollars. Its exact products, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the data supplied, and the name may be mis-read. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Mountaintop Beverage is a West Virginia manufacturer based in Morgantown that produces aseptic and extended-shelf-life beverages, including dairy, plant-based and protein drinks, for brand owners under contract. Customers are food and beverage brands and retailers, so it is a B2B co-packer. Reported funding of about 300 million dollars relates to its large production facility build-out. No consumer brand of its own, so little public awareness.

NOT A HOTEL is a Tokyo-based Japanese company that develops and sells fractional ownership of design-led villas and hotels, where owners can use their property for part of the year and the rest is operated as a hotel. Properties sit in locations such as Nasu, Hakone, Atami and Hokkaido, as well as overseas projects. Funding of about 47 billion yen is shown. Customers are affluent Japanese buyers. Niche luxury brand, mainly known in Japan.

Prestige Hospitality Ventures is the hospitality arm of Bengaluru's Prestige Group, one of India's largest real estate developers, owning and developing hotels, resorts and serviced apartments. It has partnered with operators such as Hilton, Marriott and others and has hotel assets in Bengaluru and other Indian cities. Funding of about 30 billion rupees is shown. Customers are leisure and business travellers. Parent Prestige has strong regional brand recognition in South India.

RealTruck is a Michigan-based maker and online retailer of truck and Jeep accessories, including tonneau covers (Bak, Retrax), running boards (Go Rhino), bed liners and lighting, and operates e-commerce sites such as RealTruck.com and Truck Hero. Customers are pickup and SUV owners buying online. Based in Ann Arbor with manufacturing across North America, it is owned by private equity firms including Leonard Green and Partners, and includes brands like Extang. Strong among US truck enthusiasts, with some motorsport and off-road sponsorships.

Scan.com is a London-based online marketplace for diagnostic imaging, letting patients and doctors book MRI, CT and ultrasound scans at partner clinics across the UK with reports delivered online. It sells to private patients, insurers and employers, earning a margin on each scan. Funding shown is about 287 million dollars, including debt. Modest consumer awareness in the UK private healthcare sector.

UniUni is a Canadian last-mile delivery company based in Richmond, British Columbia, providing parcel delivery for e-commerce sellers and cross-border merchants in Canada and the United States. Customers are online retailers and marketplaces shipping low-cost parcels. Funding of about 290 million dollars is shown. B2B logistics with small consumer visibility, mainly through parcels arriving at recipients.

Zoomcar is a Bengaluru-based car-sharing marketplace in India and emerging markets, connecting car owners with renters who drive themselves, with hosts earning rental income. Founded in 2013, it also operates in Egypt, Indonesia and Vietnam, and listed on Nasdaq (ZCAR) in 2023 via a SPAC merger with Innovative International Acquisition Corp. Customers are urban Indian consumers and travellers. Moderate consumer awareness in India, with a small revenue base and losses.

Advanced Digital Gaming Technology (ADGT) is a UAE-based company in Abu Dhabi, categorised under financial services and fintech, offering digital gaming technology and payment-related services. Funding of about 250 million dollars is shown. Customers and ownership are not clear from the input data, so details need checking before outreach. Likely B2B with minimal consumer brand recognition; gaming-related sectors may be restricted for sponsorship.

Citibox is a Madrid-based tech company operating smart parcel lockers installed in residential buildings and public places, so that e-commerce parcels and returns can be delivered and collected at any time. Customers are property managers, retailers and carriers across Spain, Italy, France and the UK; revenue comes from locker installations and delivery fees. Founded in 2016, it has raised about 227 million dollars. Known mainly in Spain and among property managers.

Coppel is a Mexican retailer headquartered in Culiacan, Sinaloa, founded in 1941, with over 1,000 stores selling furniture, appliances, electronics, clothing and financial services such as credit, savings and a bank, Bancoppel. It sells mostly on store credit to lower and middle-income Mexican consumers, and also operates online. Family-owned, with tens of thousands of employees and revenue in the billions of dollars. Very high consumer recognition in Mexico and a sponsor in Mexican sport, with presence in the United States too.

Country Delight is an Indian direct-to-consumer dairy and fresh food subscription brand that delivers farm-fresh milk, curd, paneer, fruit, vegetables and staples to urban households through its app. It sources from farmers and operates its own cold chain, serving customers in cities like Delhi NCR, Bengaluru and Mumbai. Founded in 2015, based in Gurugram, it has raised about 250 million dollars from investors including Temasek and Orios. Strong consumer brand in Indian cities.

Gu Ming (Guming) is a Chinese milk tea chain, established in 2010 in Zhejiang, selling tea drinks with fresh fruit and milk through thousands of franchised stores across China. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1364) in 2025. Headquartered in Wenling, with revenue largely from franchising and supplying ingredients to its stores. Highly visible in Chinese cities, with small presence outside China.

iD Fresh Food is a Bengaluru-based Indian packaged-food company known for fresh ready-to-cook idli and dosa batter, parathas, chapatis and filter coffee, sold through supermarkets and quick-commerce apps in India, the Middle East and the United States. Founded in 2005 by P.C. Musthafa and cousins, it has a large cold chain and raised about 266 million dollars, with Premji Invest as a major investor. Strong brand among urban Indian households.

INRIX is a Bellevue, Washington, provider of real-time traffic, parking and mobility data and analytics, built from billions of connected vehicle and device signals. Customers are automakers (for navigation), cities, transport agencies and businesses, and it publishes the annual Global Traffic Scorecard. Founded in 2004 as a Microsoft spin-out, it is backed by Bosch, Intel and Porsche investment arms and has raised about 264 million dollars. B2B data brand, well known in the transport industry but not to consumers.

ON TIME is the English name of Ruqi Mobility, a Guangzhou-based ride-hailing and mobile travel service backed by GAC Group, Tencent and other investors, operating electric and connected cars in Chinese cities. Customers are riders in Guangzhou and other cities, and revenue comes from fares and fleet services. Funding of about 1.9 billion yuan is shown, and the company was preparing a Hong Kong listing around 2025. Regional brand awareness within China only.

Shadowfax is a Bengaluru-based Indian logistics technology company providing last-mile delivery for e-commerce, food and quick-commerce clients such as Flipkart, Zomato, Swiggy and Meesho, using a large network of gig-economy riders. Founded in 2015, it raised about 253 million dollars and listed on the Indian stock exchanges in January 2026. B2B logistics with riders visible on the street but little consumer brand awareness.

Zevia is a Los Angeles beverage company selling zero-calorie, zero-sugar soda sweetened with stevia, in flavours such as Cola, Ginger Root Beer and Orange, plus energy drinks and mixers. Sold in grocery stores and online across the US and Canada, it listed on the NYSE (ZVIA) in 2021. Founded in 2007, with revenue around 160 million dollars. Known niche brand in the health-conscious soft drink market.

AirBoss of America is a Canadian company based in Newmarket, Ontario that makes custom rubber compounds and engineered rubber products, including mixing for tyre and mining industries, and defence products such as chemical protective gear and blast mitigation systems. Customers are tyre makers, automakers, mining firms and military buyers. Founded in 1989 and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (BOS), with revenue of several hundred million dollars. B2B with little consumer awareness.

Carwow is a London-based online car marketplace where UK and European consumers compare dealer quotes for new cars and sell their used car, and its YouTube channel of car reviews hosted by Mat Watson has a very large audience. Founded in 2010, it earns fees from dealers and manufacturers and operates in the UK, Germany, Spain and elsewhere. It has raised about 236 million dollars. Strong recognition among UK car buyers and enthusiasts, with a history of sports and motoring content sponsorship.

Kovi is a Brazilian start-up in Sao Paulo offering car subscription and rental to ride-hailing and delivery drivers, with fleets for Uber and 99 drivers as well as consumers. Customers pay weekly or monthly fees that include maintenance, insurance and tracking. Funding of about 205 million dollars has been raised. Moderate awareness among Brazilian app drivers; little elsewhere.

NaaS Technology is a Chinese electric vehicle charging services platform, formerly Newlink, operating a network of charging stations and the e-charging app Xiaoju, partnered with Alibaba's Amap for charger discovery. It listed on Nasdaq (NAAS) in 2022 via a merger, and is based in Anji, Zhejiang with roots in Beijing and Hangzhou. Customers are EV drivers and charging station operators. Brand recognition limited to Chinese EV owners; later suffered heavy losses and restructuring.

Power China (PowerChina, China Power Construction Group) is a Chinese state-owned engineering and construction giant, built around hydropower, wind, solar, grid, water and infrastructure projects at home and in dozens of countries. Based in Beijing, it is controlled by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission and listed in Shanghai (601669). Revenue exceeds 600 billion yuan. B2B and government contracts with little consumer brand awareness; some sponsorship appears in China-linked projects.

Thunder Power Holdings is an electric vehicle company with headquarters in Hong Kong, which planned to develop luxury electric vehicles and later pivoted to EV technology in Taiwan. It was set to list through a SPAC merger with Feutune Light Acquisition Corp. in 2024 and trades on Nasdaq (AIEV). Funding shown is about 199 million dollars. It has no volume vehicle production, minimal revenue and little brand awareness.

Addiante is a business consulting firm in Curitiba, Parana, Brazil, with a focus on the automotive sector according to Crunchbase. Funding shown is about 1.05 billion Brazilian reais. Services, clients and ownership are not detailed in the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Be.EV is a UK electric vehicle charging network operator based in Manchester, formerly operating as Engenie, which runs public rapid and ultra-rapid charge points and an app for drivers, and sells charging to fleets and local authorities. It describes itself as one of the largest charging networks in the UK. Funding of about 165 million pounds is shown. Customers are EV drivers and fleet operators. Moderate awareness among UK EV owners.

Lightyear was a Dutch electric vehicle start-up based in Venray, Netherlands, that developed solar-powered cars with solar roofs, including the 250,000-euro Lightyear 0 built in small numbers in Finland and the planned cheaper Lightyear 2. Customers were wealthy early adopters, and it relied on investor funding. It ran into financial difficulty, paused the Lightyear 0 in 2023 and has since been restructured or wound down, so its status should be checked. Little mainstream brand awareness but good press visibility.

Sansera Engineering is an Indian precision engineering company, listed on the NSE and BSE since 2021 and based in Bengaluru, that makes forged and machined components such as crankshafts, connecting rods and rocker arms for two-wheelers, passenger cars, commercial vehicles and aerospace. Customers include Bajaj, Maruti Suzuki, Bosch and Honda. Founded in 1981, it has factories across India and in Sweden and Thailand. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Yamaha Motor do Brasil is the Brazilian subsidiary of Yamaha Motor Co., based in Sao Paulo, selling and assembling motorcycles, outboard engines, generators and ATVs at its plant in the Manaus Free Trade Zone. It sells through a dealer network to Brazilian consumers and businesses and exports across Latin America. Part of Japan's Yamaha Motor Group, with the Yamaha brand strongly present in motorsport. Strong consumer awareness in Brazil, including MotoGP and Brazilian motorcycle racing.

LEVC (London Electric Vehicle Company) is a Coventry-based maker of the electric London taxi (the TX) and the VN5 electric van, owned by Chinese carmaker Geely, which bought the black cab maker out of administration in 2013. The TX is a range-extender hybrid electric black cab sold in the UK and overseas to taxi drivers and fleets. In 2024 it rebranded to LEVC and focused on commercial electric vehicles. Iconic London taxi design with high UK visibility.

Williams Racing is the British Formula 1 team based in Grove, near Wantage, Oxfordshire, founded in 1977 by Sir Frank Williams and Patrick Head, with nine constructors' championships and seven drivers' titles. It builds its own chassis and uses Mercedes power units. In 2020 the Williams family sold the team to US investment firm Dorilton Capital, and Atlanta-based Atlassian became title sponsor in 2025. Historic F1 brand with global recognition and an existing sponsor list; Williams Advanced Engineering also provides engineering services.

XL Fleet (now Spruce Power) was a Houston company that made electric hybrid powertrain systems for commercial fleets, listing on the NYSE via a SPAC merger with Pivotal Investment Corporation II in 2020. It later exited the fleet electrification business and bought residential solar assets, renaming itself Spruce Power Holding (SPRU) in 2022, and now owns and manages rooftop solar systems for US homeowners. Revenue is small. Limited consumer awareness.

Asahi India Glass (AIS) is a listed Indian glass manufacturer, founded in 1984 as a joint venture with Japan's Asahi Glass (AGC) and based in New Delhi, making automotive glass for carmakers such as Maruti Suzuki and Hyundai, plus float and architectural glass sold under AIS Glass Solutions with retail outlets. Revenue is over 40 billion rupees. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Automotive customers are B2B, while AIS has consumer visibility through glass retail brands in India.

Blink Charging is a US electric vehicle charging company that owns, operates and sells Level 2 and DC fast chargers across the US, Europe and Latin America, with the Blink network and the Blink Mobility app. Customers are property owners, fleets, municipalities and drivers. Founded in 2009 and based in Bowie, Maryland (previously Miami Beach), it is listed on Nasdaq (BLNK) and has made acquisitions such as SemaConnect and Blue Corner. Moderate consumer awareness among US EV drivers; persistent losses.

Damon Motors is a Vancouver-based electric motorcycle company developing high-performance smart bikes, such as the HyperSport and HyperFighter, with built-in collision warning technology. It listed on Nasdaq (DMN) via a SPAC merger with Grafiti Holding in 2024 and has taken pre-orders but delivered few motorcycles. Customers are premium motorcycle buyers. Early-stage and cash-constrained, with some media attention in the electric bike sector.

Eagers Automotive is Australia's largest automotive retailer, a listed group (ASX: APE) headquartered in Perth, Western Australia, formerly AP Eagers, with hundreds of dealerships in Australia and New Zealand across brands such as Toyota, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Ford. It expanded through the acquisition of Automotive Holdings Group in 2020. Revenue is over 10 billion Australian dollars. Customers are car buyers and fleets. Strong regional dealer brand with sponsorship of sports teams.

CEAT is an Indian tyre manufacturer, part of the RPG Group, headquartered in Mumbai, producing tyres for motorcycles, scooters, cars, SUVs, trucks, buses, tractors and off-highway vehicles. It sells in India through thousands of dealers and exports to over 100 countries, with plants in Nashik, Halol, Nagpur and Chennai. Listed on the NSE and BSE, with revenue around 130 billion rupees. Well-known consumer brand in India, strongly linked with cricket sponsorship.

Ikd is a company in Jiangbei, Chongqing, China, listed on a stock exchange, according to the input. Crunchbase industries are automotive and machinery manufacturing, and funding of about 180 million yuan is shown. Its products, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the data given, and the name may be mis-read. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Africa Finance Corporation is a multilateral development finance institution founded in 2007 by African governments and headquartered in Lagos, investing in infrastructure projects across the continent in power, transport, telecoms, heavy industry and natural resources. Member states include Nigeria and many others; it has an investment-grade rating and balance sheet of over 10 billion dollars. B2B and government-focused with little consumer brand awareness; sponsorship fit is limited to institutional visibility.

Axpo is Switzerland's largest producer of renewable energy, headquartered in Baden, a utility and energy trader owned by Swiss cantons. It generates hydropower, nuclear and renewable electricity, trades power and gas across Europe, and operates solar and wind projects. Revenue is tens of billions of Swiss francs, with sales to businesses, municipalities and consumers in Switzerland and Europe. B2B brand with moderate consumer recognition in Switzerland, known for sports sponsorship including football and ski events.

BNG Bank (Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten) is the Dutch bank of local authorities, based in The Hague, providing loans and financing to Dutch municipalities, housing associations, healthcare institutions and public bodies. It is owned by the Dutch state and municipalities and is one of the Netherlands' largest banks by balance sheet. Funding is raised on international capital markets. B2B and public sector with no consumer brand profile.

EIG Pearl Holdings is the investment vehicle through which a consortium led by US energy investor EIG acquired a 49 percent stake in Aramco Oil Pipelines Company in 2021, in a deal worth about 12.4 billion dollars, with Saudi Aramco retaining majority control. The Pearl Pipelines network carries crude oil across Saudi Arabia, and returns come from tariffs paid by Aramco under a long-term lease. Based in Dhahran. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Orsted is a Danish renewable energy company and the world's largest developer of offshore wind farms, headquartered in Fredericia (earlier Gentofte) and formerly the oil and gas firm DONG Energy. It builds and operates offshore and onshore wind, solar and storage, supplying power to utilities, corporates and governments in Europe, North America and Asia. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (ORSTED), with the Danish state as majority owner, and revenue around 70 billion Danish kroner. Mostly B2B, recognised in Denmark and the UK, with project setbacks in the US since 2023.

Pemex (Petroleos Mexicanos) is Mexico's state-owned oil and gas company, headquartered in Mexico City, that explores, refines and distributes crude oil, natural gas and petrochemicals, and operates the Pemex fuel station franchise network. It is among the world's most indebted oil companies and a large contributor to government revenue. Mexican consumers know it through its petrol stations. Employees number over 100,000. Government-owned, with a history of sponsorship in Mexican sport and motorsport, including with Sergio Perez.

PG&E is one of the largest US utilities, providing electricity and natural gas to about 16 million people across northern and central California. It is headquartered in Oakland and listed on the NYSE (PCG). The company filed for Chapter 11 in 2019 after wildfires and emerged in 2020 after compensating victims. Revenue is over 24 billion dollars. Regulated utility with high local visibility, though a reputation affected by wildfires.

SES is a Luxembourg-based satellite operator, with headquarters at Betzdorf, running geostationary and medium-earth-orbit (O3b mPOWER) fleets used for video broadcasting, data connectivity, mobility and government services. Customers include broadcasters, telecoms operators, cruise lines, airlines and defence agencies. Listed on Euronext Paris and Luxembourg (SESG), it completed the acquisition of Intelsat in 2025. Revenue is about 2 billion euros. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

ADES International Holding is a Saudi-based offshore and onshore oil and gas drilling and production services provider, headquartered in Al Khobar, operating a fleet of jack-up rigs and land rigs in the Gulf, India, Southeast Asia and elsewhere. Bank of Industry is a Nigerian development finance institution headquartered in Lagos, owned by the federal government, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Ministry of Finance Incorporated, and provides long-term loans to manufacturing, agro-processing, mining and small businesses. The Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI) is a multilateral development bank based in Tegucigalpa, Honduras, owned by Central American governments and other member countries, lending to governments and private companies for infrastructure, energy, education and economic integration. Ecobank (Ecobank Transnational Incorporated) is a pan-African banking group present in about 35 African countries, offering retail, commercial and corporate banking and payments. BWX Technologies is a US maker of nuclear components, reactors and fuel for the US Navy's submarines and aircraft carriers, as well as medical isotopes and commercial nuclear equipment. China Pacific Insurance (CPIC) is a major Chinese insurance group headquartered in Shanghai, selling life insurance (CPIC Life), property and casualty cover (CPIC P&C), health insurance and asset management to individuals and companies through agents and partners. Citizens Bank is a US regional bank headquartered in Providence, Rhode Island, and part of Citizens Financial Group (NYSE: CFG), with about 1,000 branches in 14 states across New England, the Mid-Atlantic and the Midwest, serving retail, small business and corporate clients.
