Ralliant is a US industrial technology company spun off from Fortive in mid-2025, headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, making precision instruments, sensors, test and measurement equipment and power electronics for aerospace, defence, semiconductors and industrial customers (including the Tektronix and Qualitrol businesses). Listed on the NYSE (RAL), with revenue of about 2 billion dollars. B2B with no consumer brand awareness, although Tektronix is well known to engineers.

Repsol Exploracion y Produccion (Repsol E&P) is the upstream oil and gas arm of Spanish energy group Repsol, headquartered in Madrid, exploring for and producing oil and gas in North America, Latin America, Southeast Asia, the North Sea and North Africa, with production of about 550,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Parent Repsol is listed on the Spanish stock exchange (REP). B2B upstream arm, while the Repsol brand is a household fuel and lubricants name in Spain and a long-time motorsport sponsor, including MotoGP.

SAEL is an Indian renewable energy developer based in New Delhi, building solar power projects and converting agricultural waste into biomass-based electricity. It sells power to utilities and industrial buyers and has raised funding of about 1.7 billion dollars, including debt. B2B energy company with no consumer brand awareness.

Sammaan Capital, formerly Indiabulls Housing Finance, is an Indian non-banking housing finance company based in Mumbai, offering home loans, loans against property and construction finance mainly in the affordable housing segment. Renamed in 2024 after a change in controlling ownership, with Abu Dhabi's International Holding Company (IHC) acquiring a stake in 2025. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Customers are individuals and developers across India. Moderate brand recognition in Indian lending.

San Miguel Corporation is the Philippines' largest conglomerate by sales, founded in 1890 and based in Mandaluyong, with businesses in food and beverage (San Miguel Beer, Ginebra San Miguel, Magnolia), packaging, energy (Meralco stake, power plants), infrastructure (airports, tollways) and fuel retail. Controlled by the Ramon Ang-led group, and listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (SMC). Revenue is around 1.4 trillion pesos. San Miguel Beer is a household brand with heavy sports sponsorship, including basketball.

Securing Energy for Europe (SEFE) is the German state-owned energy trading and gas supplier, formerly Gazprom Germania, placed under German trusteeship in 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine and nationalised. Headquartered in Berlin, it buys and sells gas, power and LNG for municipal utilities and industrial customers across Europe, and holds storage and infrastructure assets. Revenue is tens of billions of euros. B2B energy trader with no consumer brand awareness.

Tokopedia is an Indonesian e-commerce marketplace launched in 2009 and headquartered in Jakarta, connecting millions of small merchants and consumers, and offering payments (Tokopedia Pay), fintech, logistics and digital products. It was merged into GoTo in 2021, and in 2023 TikTok's owner ByteDance took a 75 percent controlling stake in Tokopedia as part of a deal with TikTok Shop Indonesia. Funding shown is about 2.8 billion dollars. Very high consumer awareness in Indonesia, with ASEAN sports sponsorship.

Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company (Transco) is the Houston-based interstate natural gas pipeline owned by Williams Companies (NYSE: WMB), running about 10,000 miles from south Texas to New York City and carrying roughly 15 percent of US gas demand. Customers are utilities, power generators and industrial buyers on regulated tariffs. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Triumph Group is a US aerospace company, based in Radnor, Pennsylvania, manufacturing and servicing aircraft structures, systems and components, such as landing gear, actuation and hydraulics, for Boeing, Airbus, Gulfstream and military customers. It has operated in aerospace structures and aftermarket services. Listed on the NYSE (TGI) and agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners, taking it private. B2B supplier with no consumer awareness.

Trump Media & Technology Group is the Sarasota, Florida owner of Truth Social, the social media platform launched in 2022 by Donald Trump, plus Truth+ streaming and the Truth.Fi financial brand. It listed on Nasdaq (DJT) in March 2024 via a SPAC merger with Digital World Acquisition Corp. Revenue is tiny, around 3 to 4 million dollars a year, with large losses, and a major bitcoin treasury program. Controlled by Trump. Polarising brand with limited sponsor appeal for mainstream advertisers.

Uber China was Uber's Chinese ride-hailing unit, which competed fiercely with Didi Chuxing in 2014 to 2016. In August 2016 it merged with Didi, giving Uber about 17.7 percent of the combined company in exchange for ending its China operations after huge subsidy losses. It is no longer operating as a separate business. Funding shown relates to capital invested in the unit. Historical brand, not an active sponsor prospect.

Vulcan Energy Resources is an Australian-listed (ASX: VUL) company, based in Perth, developing a combined geothermal energy and lithium extraction project in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley, planning to produce lithium hydroxide with low carbon emissions for European carmakers like Stellantis, Renault and Volkswagen. It also has offtake and funding from partners. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer brand awareness.

WEC Energy Group is a Milwaukee-based US utility holding company, listed on the NYSE (WEC), owning We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service and Peoples Gas, and serving about 4.7 million electricity and gas customers in Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan and Minnesota. Revenue is around 9 billion dollars. Customers are households and businesses. Strong regional brand recognition and a sponsor of Milwaukee sports and events.

Whitecap Resources is a Canadian oil and gas producer based in Calgary, producing about 370,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day after acquiring Veren in 2025, with assets in Alberta, Saskatchewan and British Columbia. Listed on the TSX (WCP), with a strong dividend profile. Customers are refiners and gas buyers, so B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Bloomberry Resorts is a Philippine casino resort operator, majority owned by Enrique Razon, that runs Solaire Resort & Casino in Manila's Entertainment City and Solaire North in Quezon City, with hotels, gaming, restaurants and entertainment. Listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (BLOOM). Customers are domestic and regional gamblers and tourists. Strong brand in the Philippines; as a casino operator it is restricted in some sponsorship categories.

Catena is a Swedish listed property company based in Helsingborg that develops, owns and manages logistics properties, with a portfolio in Sweden, Denmark and Finland let to retailers, distributors and 3PL operators. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (CATE), it has a property value of about 25 billion Swedish kronor. B2B real estate with no consumer brand profile.

Cencosud is a Chilean multinational retailer, based in Santiago, operating supermarkets (Jumbo, Santa Isabel, Disco, Wong), the Paris department stores, Easy home improvement, shopping centres (Costanera Center) and financial services across Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and Colombia, plus the US via The Fresh Market. Listed on the Santiago Stock Exchange (CENCOSUD), with revenue of over 15 billion dollars. Very strong consumer brands across Latin America.

Monro (Monro Muffler Brake) is a US automotive service chain, headquartered in Rochester, New York, running over 1,000 company-owned stores for tyres, brakes, oil changes and general car repair under Monro, Mr. Tire and Tire Warehouse. Listed on Nasdaq (MNRO), with revenue of about 1.2 billion dollars. Customers are motorists in the eastern and midwestern US. Well known regional automotive service brand.

Stillfront Group is a Swedish mobile and online games company, headquartered in Stockholm, owning studios and titles such as Hustle Castle, Empires & Puzzles, Imperia Online and Big Farm: Mobile Harvest, sold on iOS and Android. Customers are casual players, mostly in the US, Europe and MENA, and revenue comes from in-app purchases and ads. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SF). It grew through acquisitions with revenue of about 6 billion Swedish kronor. Games are known but the group has little consumer brand recognition.

Synovus is a US regional bank holding company, based in Columbus, Georgia, with around 250 branches across Georgia, Alabama, Florida, South Carolina and Tennessee. It offers retail, commercial, wealth and mortgage banking with assets of about 60 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (SNV), with a 2025 agreement to merge with Pinnacle Financial Partners of Nashville. Strong regional brand in the Southeast US.

Telecom Argentina is a leading Argentine telecommunications group, based in Buenos Aires, offering mobile (Personal), fixed broadband (Fibertel, Arnet), cable TV and enterprise services. It acquired Telefonica Argentina's operations in 2025 for about 1.2 billion dollars. Controlled by the Fintech and Clarin groups, and listed on the Buenos Aires exchange and NYSE (TEO). Customers are Argentine consumers and businesses. Very high household recognition in Argentina, with a record of football and sports sponsorship.

Telepass is an Italian mobility services company best known for its electronic motorway toll payment tag, now also offering parking, fuel, ride-hailing, insurance, car services and e-mobility through its apps in Italy and Europe. Based in Rome, it is 51 percent owned by Mundys (formerly Atlantia) and 49 percent by Partners Group since 2022. Customers are millions of Italian drivers and fleets. Well known household name for Italian motorists.

Wrench Group is a Marietta, Georgia, home services company providing residential heating, cooling, plumbing, electrical and appliance repair and replacement through a network of local brands across the US, formed by combining many regional service businesses. It is private equity owned and one of the largest home service providers in the country, with funding shown at about 1.3 billion dollars. Customers are homeowners. Local service brands have regional recognition; the Wrench name itself is little known.

Advanced Info Service (AIS) is Thailand's largest mobile operator, based in Bangkok, with around 45 million mobile subscribers plus AIS Fibre home broadband and enterprise services. It is majority held by Intouch Holdings and Singtel, and listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (ADVANC). Revenue is about 200 billion baht. Very high consumer brand awareness in Thailand, and an active sponsor of esports, football and entertainment.

Aihuishou (AiHuiShou, ATRenew) is a Chinese online platform for trading in and recycling used electronics such as smartphones, tablets and laptops, through its Paipai second-hand marketplace and a large network of stores. Based in Shanghai, it listed on the NYSE (RERE) in 2021. Revenue is several billion yuan. Customers are consumers selling devices and businesses buying refurbished goods. Well known in China's second-hand electronics market.

Berlin Brands Group (BBG) is a Berlin-based e-commerce group that built a portfolio of direct-to-consumer brands, such as Klarstein, Auna, Blumfeldt and Capital Sports, sold through Amazon, own sites and marketplaces in Europe, with Chinese and US sales as well. Founded in 2005, it focuses on consumer electronics, home appliances and fitness. Funding of about 1 billion dollars is shown. Brands have regional consumer recognition in Germany and Europe, though the group name is little known.

CME Group is the Chicago-based operator of the world's largest derivatives exchanges, including the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX, trading futures and options on interest rates, equities, energy, metals, agriculture and foreign exchange. It is listed on Nasdaq (CME), has revenue of over 6 billion dollars and also provides clearing. Customers are institutional traders and hedgers. Respected in finance but with little consumer awareness.

Driven Brands is the Charlotte-based owner of automotive service franchises, including Take 5 Oil Change, Meineke, Maaco, CARSTAR, ABRA, Uniban and Fix Auto, with about 5,000 locations in 15 countries. Revenue comes from franchise fees, company-owned stores and car washes, and it is listed on Nasdaq (DRVN), with Roark Capital as the largest shareholder. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. Strong US consumer brand names in car repair.

Ethiopian Airlines is Ethiopia's state-owned flag carrier and Africa's largest airline by fleet and revenue, headquartered in Addis Ababa with a hub at Bole International Airport, flying to over 140 destinations worldwide. It is a Star Alliance member and operates Boeing and Airbus fleets, with cargo, MRO and training businesses. Funding shown is about 1.1 billion dollars. Strong brand across Africa, and sponsors of sport and events.

FCMB Capital Markets is the investment banking and securities arm of First City Monument Bank in Nigeria, based in Lagos, offering advisory, debt and equity capital markets, trading and asset management for corporates and governments. It is part of FCMB Group (NGX: FCMB), a Nigerian financial group. B2B finance business with limited consumer awareness outside Nigeria.

PT DCI Indonesia is a Jakarta-based data centre operator, one of Indonesia's largest, providing colocation and cloud-ready facilities in the Jakarta area for banks, telecoms, e-commerce and government customers. Listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange (DCII) and backed by the Salim family and Toto Sugiri. Funding of about 17 trillion rupiah is shown. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Teya is a London-based payments fintech, formerly SaltPay, with roots in the Icelandic acquirer Borgun, providing card terminals, business accounts and merchant financing to small businesses in the UK, Ireland, Portugal and other European markets. It rebranded as Teya in 2023. Funding of about 1.1 billion dollars is shown, including debt. B2B brand with growing awareness among small merchants.

TORM is a Danish product tanker company, headquartered in Copenhagen and founded in 1889, owning and operating a fleet of about 80 tankers that carry refined oil products such as diesel, petrol and jet fuel around the world. Customers are oil majors and traders. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen and the NYSE (TRMD). Revenue is around 1.5 billion dollars. B2B shipping company with no consumer brand awareness.

Virgin Australia is Australia's second-largest airline, headquartered in Brisbane, flying domestic and some international routes with a leisure and business offer and the Velocity Frequent Flyer programme. It entered administration in 2020 and was bought by US private equity firm Bain Capital, relaunching as a mid-market carrier. Bain Capital reintroduced it to the ASX in 2025, with Qatar Airways taking a minority stake. Revenue is over 5 billion Australian dollars. High consumer awareness in Australia, and has sponsored motorsport and other sport in the past.

Viva Wallet is a Greek digital bank and payments fintech based in Athens, offering card acquiring, point-of-sale, online payments and business accounts to merchants across Europe. Founded in 2000 by Haris Karonis, it is a licensed bank, and JPMorgan Chase bought a 48.5 percent stake in 2022, followed by a legal dispute with the founder over its ownership and control. Funding of about 990 million dollars is shown. B2B brand with growing recognition among European small merchants.

American Hotel Income Properties (AHIP) is a Vancouver-based real estate company, TSX-listed (HOT.UN), that owned a portfolio of select-service hotels across the United States under brands such as Marriott, Hilton and IHG franchises, managed by third parties. It ran into debt trouble and sold its assets, with creditors taking control of the portfolio in 2024. B2B hotel owner, not a consumer brand, and no longer a viable sponsor candidate.

Arcelik is a Turkish home appliances manufacturer, a Koc Group company, based in Istanbul, producing white goods and consumer electronics under brands such as Beko, Grundig, Arcelik, Blomberg and Defy. It sells in more than 140 countries, with factories in Turkey, Romania, Russia and elsewhere, and combined its European business with Whirlpool's in 2024. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (ARCLK) with revenue of about 6 billion euros. Beko is a visible consumer brand with football and basketball sponsorship.

Bangkok Bank is Thailand's largest bank by assets, founded in 1944 and headquartered in Bangkok, with a large international network in Asia, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, trade finance and cross-border QR payments. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (BBL), it is controlled by the Sophonpanich family. Strong consumer brand in Thailand and across Southeast Asia, including a history of sponsorship in sport and events.

Cefetra Group is a Rotterdam-based international trader and supplier of food and feed ingredients, including grains, oilseeds, soy and animal feed raw materials, serving feed mills, food producers and farmers across Europe and beyond. It is privately owned. B2B commodity trader with no consumer brand awareness.

Chefs' Warehouse is a US specialty food distributor based in Ridgefield, Connecticut, supplying premium ingredients, proteins, pastry, cheese and imported products to restaurants, hotels, caterers and retailers, mostly in major US metropolitan areas and Canada. Listed on Nasdaq (CHEF), with revenue of about 3.5 billion dollars. Customers are chefs and foodservice operators. B2B distributor with no consumer brand awareness.

Guangdong Fenghua Advanced Technology is a Chinese electronic components maker, listed on Shenzhen (000636), producing multilayer ceramic capacitors, resistors, inductors and other passive components, plus related materials, for consumer electronics, communications, automotive and industrial customers. Based in Zhaoqing, Guangdong. B2B supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Hopper is a Montreal-based travel technology company whose mobile app predicts flight and hotel prices and recommends when to book, selling travel directly through fintech add-ons such as price freeze, cancel for any reason and a Hopper Cloud B2B arm that powers airlines and banks. Founded in 2007, it has over 100 million downloads and has raised about 730 million dollars. Strong awareness among mobile travel shoppers in North America, and heavy performance marketing.

Jushi Holdings is a US multi-state cannabis operator based in Boca Raton, Florida, running medical and adult-use dispensaries under the Beyond/Hello, The Bank and Nature's Remedy names in Pennsylvania, Illinois, Virginia, Nevada and elsewhere, and producing branded cannabis products. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (JUSH). Customers are cannabis consumers and patients. Regional retail brands, and cannabis marketing restrictions generally limit sponsorship.

SGS is a Swiss inspection, verification, testing and certification company, headquartered in Geneva (Crunchbase shows Baar), founded in 1878 as a grain inspection firm, with about 100,000 employees and 2,600 offices and labs worldwide. Customers are manufacturers, retailers, governments and commodity traders, and revenue is about 6.6 billion Swiss francs. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (SGSN). B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though well known among suppliers and importers.

Xpansiv is a New York-based market infrastructure and data company that runs the CBL exchange for environmental commodities, including carbon credits, renewable energy certificates and other sustainability instruments, with data and registry services for traders and corporates. Customers are energy companies, corporates and financial institutions buying and retiring offsets. Backed by institutional investors, with funding of about 718 million dollars shown. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

ABB E-Mobility is the electric vehicle charging division of Swiss technology group ABB, making DC fast chargers (Terra series), AC wallboxes and charging software for fleets, charge point operators and automakers, with manufacturing in Europe, the US and China. ABB itself is based in Zurich and listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and NYSE (ABB). The Crunchbase industry label is inaccurate. B2B charging hardware supplier; ABB is well known, and has a Formula E title sponsorship history.

Alloha Fibra is a Brazilian fibre broadband provider based in Sao Paulo, selling internet access to homes and businesses and holding regional internet service providers. It has raised funding of about 640 million dollars, including debt. Customers are Brazilian households. Regional telecom brand with limited recognition beyond its service areas.

Conigital is a UK driverless vehicle and transport technology company based in Birmingham, working on autonomous vehicle software and connected mobility, with research programmes involving universities. Funding of about 628 million dollars is shown, which seems unusually high and may reflect an OCR error. B2B technology business with little public brand awareness.

Dapper Labs is a Vancouver-based blockchain company that built the Flow blockchain and consumer products including CryptoKitties, NBA Top Shot and NFL All Day, selling digital collectibles under licences from sports leagues. Founded in 2018, it has raised over 600 million dollars at a peak valuation of about 7 billion dollars in 2021, but the NFT market has since fallen sharply. Strong awareness among sports-collectible and crypto audiences, with licensed deals with the NBA and NFL.

dLocal is a Montevideo-based payments company that lets global merchants such as Amazon, Spotify and Uber accept local payment methods and make payouts in emerging markets across Latin America, Africa and Asia. Founded in 2016, it listed on Nasdaq (DLO) in 2021, processing tens of billions of dollars a year. B2B payments infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

Getlink is the French listed group (Euronext Paris: GET) that operates the Channel Tunnel, including the Eurotunnel Le Shuttle car and truck service, and runs Europorte rail freight, ElecLink electricity interconnector and Eurotunnel Freight. Based in Paris, with revenue of about 1.8 billion euros. Customers are motorists, hauliers and rail operators between the UK and France. Eurotunnel is a well-known travel brand in the UK and France.

HEA Energy is an Abu Dhabi-based offshore marine logistics company supporting the energy industry with vessels and offshore support services. Funding shown is about 550 million dollars. Customers are oil and gas operators in the Gulf. B2B with no consumer brand awareness; limited information on ownership.

Pensana is a UK-listed rare earths company based in London, developing the Longonjo project in Angola and a rare earth processing hub at Saltend in Hull, aiming to supply magnet rare earth oxides such as neodymium and praseodymium. Customers are magnet makers and electric vehicle supply chains. It has raised funding of about 560 million dollars including debt facilities. B2B mining and processing with no consumer brand awareness.

QVC Group (formerly Qurate Retail) is a US video and online commerce group, headquartered in West Chester, Pennsylvania, operating the QVC and HSN television shopping networks, Zulily and Cornerstone brands such as Ballard Designs and Frontgate. It sells home, fashion, beauty and jewellery to consumers through TV, web and apps. Listed on Nasdaq (QVCGA). Revenue has declined to around 10 billion dollars. Well known in the US among home shoppers.

Rotterdam World Gateway (RWG) is the container terminal at Maasvlakte 2 in the Port of Rotterdam, operated as a joint venture of DP World, Hutchison Ports, MOL and HMM. It is a highly automated deep-sea terminal handling mega container ships for shipping lines. Funding shown is about 500 million euros. B2B logistics with no consumer brand awareness.

SAL (Saudi Airlines Cargo) is the Jeddah-based Saudi air cargo and logistics company, a subsidiary of Saudia Group, offering air freight, ground handling, warehousing and logistics services at Saudi airports. It was listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in 2022. Funding shown is about 2.5 billion riyals. B2B logistics with little consumer awareness.

SalMar is a Norwegian salmon farmer, one of the world's largest, producing Atlantic and organic salmon from farms along Norway's coast and in Iceland, with its own processing plants. Based in Frøya (Crunchbase shows Kverva), it sells to retailers and food processors in Europe, Asia and the US. Listed on Oslo Bors (SALM), with revenue of about 20 billion Norwegian kroner. Mostly B2B, with limited consumer recognition.

Shenzhen MTC is a company based in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, that Crunchbase describes as specialising in the production of consumer electronics. Funding of about 4.4 billion yuan is shown. Its specific products, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the data supplied. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

WHSmith is a British retailer, historically known for its high street stores, newspapers, stationery and books. It sold its high street chain in 2025 to Modella Capital and now operates as a travel retailer, with stores in airports, railway stations, hospitals and motorway services in the UK, North America, Australia and elsewhere. Based in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange (SMWH), founded in 1792. Very high UK consumer recognition.

Current is a New York mobile banking platform offering checking accounts through partner banks, early direct deposit, savings pods and credit-building tools, mainly for younger and lower-income customers. Founded in 2015, it has raised about 680 million dollars and claims millions of members. Revenue comes from interchange fees and subscriptions. Known to US neobank users, with limited broader awareness.

Academy Sports + Outdoors is a US sporting goods and outdoor retailer based in Katy, Texas, with about 300 large stores across the South and Midwest selling hunting, fishing, camping, apparel, footwear and team sports gear, plus an online store. Founded in 1938, it listed on Nasdaq (ASO) in 2020, after private equity ownership by KKR. Revenue is about 6 billion dollars. Strong regional consumer brand with significant sports marketing and team partnerships.

Allica Bank is a UK digital bank for established small and medium-sized businesses, founded in 2018 and based in London, offering business current accounts, savings, commercial mortgages and asset finance, with a banking licence granted in 2019. It reached unicorn status after raising funding of over 500 million dollars. Customers are UK SMEs, and the brand is known in the UK business banking community with marketing aimed at business owners.

Chelsea Football Club is the London Premier League club, based at Stamford Bridge, with two Champions League titles (2012, 2021) and a Club World Cup in 2025. It has been owned since 2022 by the BlueCo consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital. Revenue comes from broadcasting, matchday and commercial sponsorship, including deals with Nike, Infinite Athlete and Chelsea's women's team. Revenue is about 500 million pounds. Huge global fan base and an elite sports sponsorship property.

Chord Music Partners is a New York-based independent music rights company that buys and manages catalogues of songs and recordings, earning royalties from streaming, radio and licensing. Funding of about 500 million dollars is shown, likely mostly capital for catalogue acquisitions. Customers are songwriters and music users. B2B investor in rights with no consumer brand awareness.

Kashable is a New York fintech that offers affordable loans to employees through employers, with repayments by payroll deduction, aimed at workers with limited access to credit. Customers are employers who offer the benefit and employees who borrow. Funding of about 473 million dollars is shown, which includes debt capital for lending. B2B2C brand with little awareness outside HR and benefits teams.

Lotus Technology is the electric vehicle arm of Lotus, the British sports car brand owned by China's Geely and listed on Nasdaq (LOT) via SPAC in 2024. Headquartered in Wuhan, it sells the Eletre SUV, Emeya GT and Evija hypercar, with R&D in Hethel, England. Revenue is about 800 million dollars, with large losses. Strong global brand recognition thanks to Lotus's racing heritage and Formula 1 history, and highly relevant to motorsport marketing.

Rockley Photonics was a Pasadena, California, silicon photonics company that developed spectroscopic sensing chips to measure biomarkers such as blood pressure and glucose in wearables, with Apple as its major customer. It listed on the NYSE through a SPAC merger in 2021, struggled commercially, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023. No longer an active independent business.

Slice is an Indian fintech, formerly a credit card and consumer lending start-up, headquartered in Bengaluru, that offered small loans and a payment card. It merged with North East Small Finance Bank in 2024, becoming a digital-first small finance bank known as slice Small Finance Bank, regulated by the Reserve Bank of India. Customers are young Indian consumers. Strong awareness among young app users, with active marketing.

Zum is a Redwood City, California, school transportation company that provides student buses and routing technology for school districts in the United States, including electric school buses, and also offers child care transport. Founded in 2014, it has contracts with large districts such as Oakland and Seattle, and has raised funding of about 500 million dollars. Customers are school districts and parents. Local brand recognition among families in its districts.

Bharat Forge is an Indian engineering company, part of the Kalyani Group, based in Pune, that makes forged and machined components for cars, trucks, aerospace, energy and defence, and is one of the world's largest forging firms. It has plants in India, Germany, the US, Sweden and elsewhere. Listed on the NSE and BSE (BHARATFORG), with revenue of over 150 billion rupees. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness, though it supports Indian defence and motorsport links.

Caliceo is a French family-owned group of aquatic wellness and fitness centres, based in Sainte-Foy-les-Lyon near Lyon, operating thermal-style spa and swimming-based clubs with pools, spas and fitness areas. Customers are French leisure users paying memberships or day entry. Funding shown is about 342 million euros. Regional French consumer brand.

ecoATM is a San Diego company that operates thousands of self-service kiosks, mostly in shopping centres and Walmart stores, where consumers sell used smartphones, tablets and other devices for instant cash. It resells and recycles the devices, and is part of the ecoATM Gazelle group. Customers are consumers looking to trade in devices and wholesale buyers of refurbished electronics. Well known kiosk brand in the US, with a sustainability angle.

Ithaca Energy is an independent North Sea oil and gas producer based in Aberdeen, producing about 100,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day from fields such as Captain, Alba, Erskine and Cygnus, and listed on the London Stock Exchange (ITH) since 2022. Delek Group of Israel holds a majority stake. It acquired Eni's UK assets in 2024. Customers are refiners and gas buyers. B2B energy producer with no consumer brand awareness.

Leejam Sports is the Saudi Arabia fitness chain operating the Fitness Time brand, with about 150 gyms for men and women across the Kingdom, and listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul: 1830). Based in Riyadh, it earns membership fees and personal training and retail revenue from several hundred thousand members. Revenue is about 1.5 billion riyals. Strong consumer brand in Saudi Arabia and a sponsor of Saudi sports and events.

Prestige Consumer Healthcare is a US marketer of over-the-counter healthcare brands, such as Monistat, Dramamine, Summer's Eve, Clear Eyes, Chloraseptic and BC/Goody's powders, sold in drugstores and supermarkets. It does not manufacture, using contract manufacturers. Based in Tarrytown, New York, and listed on the NYSE (PBH), it has revenue of about 1.1 billion dollars. Customers are US consumers; products have strong shelf presence in pharmacies, but the corporate name is little known.

Vermont Transco is a Vermont electric transmission company that owns and operates the high-voltage transmission network in the state, owned by Vermont utilities including Green Mountain Power and Vermont Electric Power Company, with Central Vermont Public Service as a legacy owner. It earns regulated transmission revenue. Based in Rutland. B2B regulated infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Viveo is a company based in Sao Paulo, Brazil, which according to Crunchbase manufactures and distributes materials and products in the fitness and health care sectors. Funding of about 2.07 billion Brazilian reais is shown. Its brands, customers and ownership are not specified in the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

West Marine is a US boating supplies retailer, headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, with around 200 stores plus online sales of marine electronics, safety gear, parts and apparel, serving recreational boaters and fishers. Founded in 1968 in California, it has been owned by private equity firm Monomoy Capital Partners since 2017. Strong consumer brand among US boaters, with relevant motorsport and marine event sponsorship.

Yamaha Motor Finance Corporation, USA is the finance arm of Yamaha Motor in the US, based in Cypress, California, providing retail loans, floor plan financing and extended service contracts for customers and dealers of Yamaha motorcycles, ATVs, marine products and golf cars. It is a subsidiary of Yamaha Motor Co. (Japan) and part of the Yamaha Motor Corporation USA. Strong brand association with Yamaha, with a company well known for motorsport.

HealthKart is an Indian health and nutrition company that sells dietary supplements, protein products and sports nutrition through its own brands MuscleBlaze, HK Vitals and Gritzo, and operates the HealthKart online marketplace. Based in Gurugram, it was founded in 2011 and has raised about 350 million dollars from investors including Temasek and Kae Capital. Customers are Indian fitness enthusiasts and families. MuscleBlaze is a strong fitness brand in India with athlete endorsements.

Mitti, by SafetyCulture, is described by Crunchbase as the operations system for the frontline, providing mobile tools for inspections, checklists and asset management. SafetyCulture is a Sydney-based software company (iAuditor) with customers across construction, retail and hospitality. Funding of about 355 million dollars is shown. B2B software with little consumer brand awareness.

Sidecar Health is a Manhattan Beach, California, health insurtech offering employer health plans that pay members a fixed price for services using real-time pricing technology, instead of narrow provider networks. Founded in 2018, it has raised about 330 million dollars. Customers are employers and their employees in the US. Low consumer brand awareness.

Tsu was a social network launched in 2014 that shared advertising revenue with its users, drawing early controversy over its payment scheme. It never grew into a major platform and has been largely inactive. The Crunchbase entry shows funding of about 360 million dollars, which looks unusually high and likely incorrect. Not a viable sponsorship prospect.

Zigbang is a South Korean real estate platform, based in Seoul, whose app lists apartments, studios and houses for rent and sale, and provides property data, virtual tours and agent tools. Founded in 2007, it has been a market leader among smaller homes and one-room rentals, and holds a large user base of young renters. Funding of about 430 billion won is shown. Strong consumer brand in Korea, with heavy advertising.

Aegean Airlines is Greece's largest airline, based in Kifisia near Athens, flying scheduled and charter routes across Europe and the Mediterranean, and a Star Alliance member since 2010. It acquired Olympic Air in 2013 and operates a fleet of Airbus aircraft. Listed on the Athens Stock Exchange (AEGN), with revenue of over 1.5 billion euros and about 15 million passengers a year. Very high consumer visibility in Greece, with a history of sports sponsorship.

Lendingkart is an Ahmedabad-based Indian fintech that provides working capital loans to small businesses, using data and digital underwriting to approve loans quickly, with customers across India. Founded in 2014, it raised funding of about 326 million dollars from investors including Fullerton Financial, Bertelsmann India and Mayfield. Awareness is mostly among small business owners in India.
